Holding a tuft of hair, Muawiya said the Prophet forbade false hair, saying the Israelites were destroyed when their women used it.
Among earlier peoples were persons inspired with what came true, and if the Prophet's followers have any, it is Umar bin Al-Khattab.
An Israelite who had murdered ninety-nine was forgiven dying on his way to repent; a cow and a wolf spoke; land buyer and seller each refused gold found buried there.
Plague was a punishment on Israelites or earlier people and a mercy for believers: do not enter or flee a plague land, and one staying patiently gets a martyr's reward.
Rebuking Usama's intercession for a Makhzumi woman who stole, the Prophet said earlier nations perished by sparing nobles, and he would cut off even Fatima's hand if she stole.
Two men recited a verse differently; displeased at their dispute, the Prophet said both were correct and they should not differ, for nations before them differed and were destroyed.
The Prophet told of a prophet whose people beat him bloody, who wiped his face saying: O Allah, forgive my nation, for they have no knowledge.
Allah forgave men who, fearing Him, had their bodies burnt and scattered after death, and a lender who told his servant to forgive poor debtors so Allah might forgive them.
A woman entered the Fire because of a cat she imprisoned until it died, neither feeding it nor setting it free to find food.
Among the sayings of earlier prophets that people still have: if you do not feel ashamed, then do whatever you like.
A man walking in pride with his garment dragging was swallowed by the earth and will go on sinking in it until the Day of Resurrection.
Muslims, last to come, will be foremost at the Resurrection; earlier nations differed over Friday, Saturday going to the Jews and Sunday to the Christians; Muslims must bathe weekly.
On his last visit to Medina Muawiya showed a tuft of false hair in a sermon, saying the Prophet called the practice falsehood.
Ibn Abbas explains that in verse 49.13 Shu'ub means the large nations and Qabail the branch tribes.
Asked who is the most honourable of people, the Prophet said the most righteous, and when they said that was not their question, Joseph, the prophet of Allah.
Zainab bint Abi Salama confirms that the Prophet was of the tribe of Mudar, descended from An-Nadr bin Kinana, and reports his ban on four kinds of wine vessels.
People differ in nature: the best before Islam are the best in Islam if they understand religion, the best hate ruling most, and the worst is the double-faced.
Quraish lead in ruling, Muslims following their Muslims and disbelievers their disbelievers; the best hate ruling; Ibn Abbas says verse 42.23 asks Quraish to keep their kinship with the Prophet.
Afflictions come from the east; rudeness and pride mark the camel-herding bedouins of Rabi'a and Mudar, calmness the owners of sheep, while belief and wisdom are Yemenite.
Angered at talk of a king from Qahtan, Muawiya cited the Prophet: ruling stays with Quraish while they keep the religion; another report adds, even if only two remain.
The Prophet told Uthman that Bani Hashim and Bani Al-Muttalib are one, and Aisha treated women of Bani Zuhra kindly for their relation to the Prophet.
Quraish, the Ansar, Juhaina, Muzaina, Aslam, Ashja' and Ghifar are the Prophet's disciples, with no protector except Allah and His Apostle.
Aisha vowed never to speak to Abdullah bin Az-Zubair for wanting to stop her charity; the Prophet's Zuhri uncles won her over, and she freed forty slaves in expiation.
Uthman had Zaid bin Thabit and three Quraishis copy the Quran, telling them to write in the language of Quraish where they differed, as it was revealed in it.
Passing men of Aslam at archery, the Prophet told the children of Ishmael to shoot, their father being an archer, and said he was with both teams.
Knowingly claiming a false father is disbelief and a false people earns the Fire; such claims, invented dreams and sayings falsely ascribed to the Prophet are among the worst lies.
The Abd al-Qais delegation of Rabi'a, cut off by Mudar's disbelievers, are told to believe in Allah, pray, pay Zakat, give a fifth of booty and avoid four vessels.
From the pulpit the Prophet pointed east, saying afflictions will start from there, where the side of Satan's head comes out.
Quraish, the Ansar, Juhaina, Muzaina, Aslam, Ghifar and Ashja' are the Prophet's helpers; he prayed for Ghifar and Aslam and ranked them above Tamim, Asad, Ghatafan and Amir.
The Hour will not be established until a man from Qahtan appears, driving the people with his stick.
The Prophet condemned the call of Ignorance when an emigrant and Ansari quarrelled, refused to kill Ibn Ubai, and disowned whoever slaps his face, tears his dress or so calls.
Amr bin Luhai, father of Khuza'a, was seen dragging his intestines in the Fire as the first to free animals for false gods, and the Bahira and Saiba are explained.
Abu Dhar of Ghifar tells how Ali secretly led him to the Prophet in Mecca, where he embraced Islam and was twice beaten for declaring it, Al-Abbas shielding him.
Aslam, Ghifar and some of Muzaina and Juhaina are better with Allah than the tribes of Asad, Tamim, Hawazin and Ghatafan.
Ibn Abbas points to the verses after 6.130, on those who killed their children in folly and forbade what Allah provided, to show the ignorance of the Arabs.
When told to warn his near kindred, the Prophet called each tribe of Quraish by name, telling Bani Abd Manaf, his aunt and Fatima to buy themselves from Allah.
Asking the Ansar whether any stranger was among them, the Prophet said the son of a people's sister belongs to them.
During the days of Mina the Prophet stopped Abu Bakr rebuking two girls beating drums, as these were Eid days, and let Ethiopians play in the mosque while Aisha watched.
Seeking to satirise the infidels, Hassan bin Thabit would draw the Prophet out of their lineage like a hair from dough; Aisha forbade abusing him, for he defended the Prophet.
The Prophet's five names include Al-Mahi, Al-Hashir and Al-Aqib, no prophet after him; Quraish curse Mudhammam, not Muhammad; he is the last brick completing the prophets' house.
